title: Claude 5 Family: Fable 5, Sonnet 5, Opus 5
content:
## Overview

In summer 2026, Anthropic replaced the Claude 4.x lineup with the **Claude 5 family**, shipping three models in under two months: **Fable 5** (June 9), **Sonnet 5** (June 30), and **Opus 5** (July 24). Rather than a single flagship launch, this was a portfolio rollout — each model targets a different budget and workload, and Anthropic has signaled this faster, staggered cadence is the new norm rather than an exception.

---

## Claude Fable 5 (June 9, 2026)

Fable 5 is Anthropic's new top-of-line-plus-safety tier. It shares its underlying model with **Claude Mythos 5**, Anthropic's raw frontier model, but Fable 5 carries additional safeguards specifically for biology, cybersecurity, and LLM R&D dual-use risks — the model most likely to be asked genuinely dangerous questions, wrapped in the most conservative safety layer.

Those safeguards were a moving target through the summer: an August 2026 update improved Fable 5's biology safeguards, cutting biology-related **false-positive fallbacks by about 85%**, so the model now answers a much wider range of benign biology, health, and educational questions while still blocking genuine dual-use requests.

**Subscription access** (finalized July 20, 2026): Max and Team Premium plans keep Fable 5 included at up to 50% of weekly usage limits. Pro and Team Standard plans moved to metered usage credits instead of flat inclusion.

---

## Claude Sonnet 5 (June 30, 2026)

Sonnet 5 is the mid-tier workhorse, positioned as an upgrade to Sonnet 4.6 with a big jump in agentic coding and everyday professional work (drafting, spreadsheets, presentations).

**Specs and pricing:**

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Context window | 1,000,000 tokens |
| Max output | 128K tokens |
| Input price | $2 / 1M tokens (until Aug 31, 2026, then $3) |
| Output price | $10 / 1M tokens (then $15) |
| Reasoning effort | Selectable: low, medium, high, max, x-high |

**Benchmarks:** 91.1% on GPQA Diamond, 71.5% on the Coding Index, 55.3% on the Intelligence Index, and 63.2% on SWE-bench Pro.

Sonnet 5 introduced **adaptive thinking** — reasoning effort is now a selectable parameter rather than an on/off toggle, letting callers trade latency and cost against reasoning depth per request. It also supports vision, tool calling, prompt caching, web search, structured (JSON schema) outputs, and computer use.

---

## Claude Opus 5 (July 24, 2026)

Opus 5 closed out the family, described by Anthropic as coming close to Fable 5's frontier intelligence at roughly half the price, while matching Opus 4.8's cost for a large capability jump. The positioning: a "thoughtful and proactive" model for complex reasoning and long-horizon agentic work, without Fable 5's extra safety-layer latency.

---

## Naming and positioning shift

The Claude 5 generation drops the old Haiku/Sonnet/Opus-only structure's strict three-tier symmetry by adding **Fable** as a fourth, safety-hardened tier above Opus (with **Mythos** as its unrestricted sibling, not broadly available). As of this generation, the fastest/cheapest tier is still filled by **Haiku 4.5** — Anthropic did not ship a Haiku 5 alongside the June–July releases, so Haiku 4.5 remains the current lightweight option sitting underneath Sonnet 5 and Opus 5.

---

## Why it matters

- **Staggered releases over a single flagship drop** — Anthropic can now ship a new price/capability point every few weeks instead of once or twice a year.
- **Adaptive reasoning effort** turns "thinking mode" from a binary switch into a tunable dial, which matters for cost-sensitive production agents.
- **Fable 5's safety-fallback fix** (85% fewer false positives) shows Anthropic actively tuning dual-use safeguards post-launch based on real usage, not just at model release.
